newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia minister rejects international peace talks.
newsitem.headline: Colombia minister rejects international peace talks.

text.p: Colombia's Foreign Relations Minister Maria Emma Mejia on Tuesday rejected a former Costa Rican president's impassioned plea for international peace talks to end more than three decades of conflict in Colombia.

At a conference on violence, which opened over the weekend in the Colombian beach resort town of Cartagena, Nobel Peace Prize-winner Oscar Arias urged the government and leftist guerrillas to negotiate an end to the spiral of violence with the help of international mediators.

Rebels unleashed one of their bloodiest offensives in recent memory a month ago, and there appears to be little appetite on either side to declare an end to hostilities. In the past, peace talks in Mexico and Venezuela involving the government and Colombia's two largest surviving guerrilla armies collapsed.

In comments to the press on Tuesday, Mejia said: "We don't think we need the type of international mediation (that Arias is suggesting). We've got the cooperation we think is necessary at the moment."
